description: How design-render resolves a theme's font stack and which metrics it lays text out with. For the html target a requested family first resolves to the licensed faces the theme itself ships, declared in the theme's assets/fonts/faces.json with family, weight, file, format, advance_em and licence, which the page embeds, each under its weight; otherwise it resolves only to a face bundled here or to a generic family below, and every other family is skipped and recorded as a substitution. The PPTX target embeds no font and names a typeface rather than a family keyword, so it skips a theme-shipped family and each generic family also documents the Office typeface a deck is written in. references/design-render.md explains the algorithm.

system-ui.note: The platform's interface face, with the platform's sans-serif as its own fallback.

monospace.note: The platform's default monospace face; every glyph advances the same width.

resolution_order: Walk the requested stack in order.

For the html target only, a family the theme ships in assets/fonts/faces.json resolves to its faces: layout measures with the declared advance_em of the face matched for weight 400, and the page embeds every face of the family under its declared weight; bundled_faces and the generic families come after it.
A family bundled in bundled_faces resolves to that face.
A generic family keyword resolves to its documented chain.
Any other family is skipped and recorded; the first resolvable member wins.
A stack with no resolvable member fails as font-unresolved, naming its first family.

The PPTX target writes a resolved generic family as its pptx_typeface, which Office ships, and records it in the deck's manifest beside the requested family; it embeds no font, so a theme-shipped family is skipped there and recorded as a substitution.
